title: Job 6
paragraphs: ¹ Then Job replied: ² "If only my anguish could be weighed and all my misery placed on the scales! ³ It would surely outweigh the sand of the seas — no wonder my words have been rash. ⁴ The arrows of the Almighty have pierced me; my spirit drinks in their poison; God's terrors are marshaled against me. ⁵ Does a wild donkey bray when it has grass? Does an ox bellow when it has feed?

⁶ Can bland food be eaten without salt? Is there any taste in the white of an egg? ⁷ My appetite refuses to touch such things; they are like disgusting food to me. ⁸ Oh, that I might have what I ask for, that God would grant what I hope for — ⁹ that he would be willing to crush me, to let loose his hand and cut me off! ¹⁰ Then I would still have this comfort, this joy even in relentless pain: that I had not denied the words of the Holy One.

¹¹ What strength do I have to go on hoping? What future awaits me that I should be patient? ¹² Is my strength the strength of stone? Is my body made of iron? ¹³ Do I have any power to help myself, now that every resource has been driven from me? ¹⁴ A desperate man should have the devotion of his friends, even if he abandons the fear of the Almighty. ¹⁵ But my brothers have been as treacherous as a seasonal stream, as the courses of streams that run dry,

¹⁶ dark from melting ice and swollen with snowmelt, ¹⁷ but that vanish in the heat and disappear in the warmth. ¹⁸ Caravans turn aside from their routes; they go up into the wasteland and perish. ¹⁹ The caravans of Tema look for water; the traveling merchants of Sheba hope to find it. ²⁰ They are disappointed because they had been confident; they arrived there only to be let down.

²¹ Now you too have proved to be nothing — you see something dreadful and you pull back in fear. ²² Have I ever said, 'Give me something'? Have I asked you, 'Pay a bribe on my behalf'? ²³ Or, 'Rescue me from the hand of the enemy'? Or, 'Deliver me from the grip of ruthless men'? ²⁴ Teach me, and I will be silent; show me where I have been wrong. ²⁵ How painful honest words can be! But what do your arguments prove?

²⁶ Do you think you can reprove my words as though they were just wind? You would even cast lots for the fatherless and make merchandise of your own friend. ²⁷ Are you plotting to criticize me? Would you even cast lots over an orphan and barter away your friend? ²⁸ But now please look at me — would I lie to your face? ²⁹ Relent, do not be unjust; reconsider, for my integrity is at stake. ³⁰ Is there any injustice on my tongue? Can my mouth not discern wickedness?
